描述_ZN: The Landscape Album, Ming, painted by Dong Qichang, 7vo, paper, color on paper, 26 cm long, 20.4 cm wide; 24.8 cm long, 24.8 cm wide.　　In the first panel, the title of this panel reads: "The immortal guest of Ji Xian asks about his career, and buys a fishing boat to spend his years. The case has Huangting Zun has wine, and the place with less storm is home. Xuanzai complements the picture." Inscription: "Qichang" seal. Inscriptions of "Song Eun's review", "Gala in Xin's", "Yi Jin Zhai seal" and "Huang XI Zi".　　The composition of the painting takes the potential of the corners, with hills and ravines, jungles, huts and villages, winding mountain paths and open water. A flat boat slowly coming, relaxed and comfortable. The brushwork and ink are light, and the chalking and dyeing are exquisite.　　In the second panel, the title of the painting reads: "The water of Nanling is long and lingering, the wind is tight and the clouds are busy, and it wants to change into autumn. The wind is tight and the clouds are full of autumn. It is a lonely place for a guest's heart, who has red sleeves leaning on a high building. Xuanzai." Inscription: "Qichang" seal. Inscriptions of "Song Eun's review" and "Jiang Shang Wai Shi".　　The wide water surface divides the picture into distant and near scenes, with rocks and trees on the near side and reeds moving with the wind, while the man in the building looks at the mountains across the river from afar, seeing only green hills and green islands, and clouds and smoke flowing. The whole picture is about the brushwork, mostly painted with a medium sharpness, the mountains and rocks are chapped in a complicated but not chaotic way, and the rules are self-existing. The coloring is pure and elegant, not too rich and beautiful, which better expresses the literati's interest.　　The third opening, this panel is inscribed: "Imitating half of Beiyuan's mountain and stream travel. Xuanzai." Inscription: "Dong Qichang". Inscriptions of "Jiang Shang Wai Shi" and "Song Eminent Review".　　The picture represents the scene of the towering boulders in the mountains and ten thousand trees competing for beauty, and the thick texture of the mountains and rocks is painted with different shades of ink, and the strokes are connected with each other, using both dryness and wetness, with the flavor of Dong Yuan in the Fifth Dynasty.　　　　　　The fourth panel is inscribed: "The air clears the surface of the earth and the clouds converge at the end of the sky. The waves of the cave are beginning, and the leaves of the wood are slightly removed. Xuanzai." Inscription: "Qichang" seal. Inscriptions of "Gala Chongguang Seal", "Jiang Shang Wai Shi" and "Song Eminent Review".　　A few trees are on the near bank, while the flat slope and gentle hills in the distance are hidden by green hills. The mountains are dotted with horizontal strokes of moss, resembling the charm of Xiaomi (Mi Youren). The picture presents a quiet and elegant atmosphere, and the composition is sparse, with the brushwork of Ni Zan.　　In the fifth panel, the painting is inscribed, "Imitating the brushwork of Beiyuan. Xuanzai." Inscription: "Seal of Dong Qichang". Inscriptions: "Reviewed by Song eminent" and "Jiang Shangguang".　　In the picture, the path is winding, trees are scattered, and several huts are vaguely revealed among the rocks. The rocks are mostly chiseled with long strokes, and the branches of the trees are sketched with strokes, and the leaves are dyed with ink dots. The brushwork does not seek to work in detail, but to seek the innocent interest.　　The sixth panel is inscribed: "The sea breeze keeps blowing, and the moon shines on the river (this word is removed by dots). Xuanzai." Inscription: "Qichang" seal. Inscriptions: "Jiang Shang Wai Shi" and "Song Eminent Review".　　The painting is a partial interception of a landscape, with beautiful green peaks and waterfalls hanging upside down, which makes people feel relaxed and happy.　　In the seventh panel, this panel is inscribed: "Imitating the brushwork of Huang Zijiu's giant scroll landscape in the collection of Bachelor Hua of Liangxi. Xuanzai." Inscription: "Seal of Dong Qichang". Inscriptions: "Reviewed by Song eminent" and "Jiang Shangguang".　　The forms are drawn with light ink lines, and the mountains and rivers are written with fine and moist lines, while the recumbent brush with moss dots and the pistachio chap are used by Huang Gongwang in the Yuan Dynasty. The pine trees are both thick and light, with a distinction between near and far. This huge brushwork is not constrained in the small painting format, Dong's random brushwork has a natural interest.　　For the study of painting, Dong Qichang believed that one should first take the ancients as teachers, copy their paintings carefully, and integrate their brushwork techniques and layouts and compositions in one's mind, so as to gain the interest of the ancients' brushwork and ink, and from this seven-page album, one can appreciate Dong's brushwork and ink skills. The author has taken the strengths of the brush and ink of various schools, and then applied his own knowledge and insight to change them, showing the extraordinary charm of expressing his thoughts and creating a unique style, which has been beyond the reach of many later painters who have copied ancient times.　　It is recorded in Guan Guan Guanjun's "Sanqiu Ge Shu and Painting Records" (Vol. 1).
